metadata.title: Temperature prediction on Civaux Wall during hydration

source.cited_in: Pesavento et al., Chapter 7, Fig. 7.1, RILEM SOA 27, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-76617-1_7

metadata.validation_method: comparison with 6 embedded temperature sensors + 1 external sensor
metadata.validation_target: Temperature history at gage points over ~140 h of hydration (Fig. 7.1)
metadata.notes: Thermal inputs now taken from the CEOS.fr THM benchmark dataset reproduced in Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux': geometry (Sec. IV.A + Fig. IV-11a), h (Annexe C.1), k/cp/mix (Annexe C.2), Ea (Tableau IV-3). STILL UNCALIBRATED: affinity kinetics B1/B2. STILL SIMPLIFIED: the radier is not modelled (adiabatic bottom), so sonde-1/2 level gages run hot -- Briffaut notes the same limitation for sonde 1. Pure thermo-chemo; no mechanics simulated.
metadata._comment_height_ambiguity: UNRESOLVED, AFFECTS EVERY GAGE Y-COORDINATE. The real wall is: 0.40 m foundation (radier) + lift 1 = 1.90 m + lift 2 = 0.90 m, lift 2 cast at ~168 h. This model is ONE 1.2 x 2.4 m block cast at t=0. Its 2.4 m height matches NEITHER lift 1 alone (1.90 m) NOR the full wall (2.80 m). Since t_end = 140 h < 168 h, the modelled block can only physically represent LIFT 1, whose height is 1.90 m -> the domain height is most likely wrong and should be 1.90 m. Consequence: gage_core / gage_surface at y = 1.20 sit at mid-height of the 2.4 m block but at 63% of a real 1.90 m lift. They stay in the lift-1 interior either way, so the SONDE ASSIGNMENT is unaffected; only the absolute heights are. NOT changed here -- that is a modelling decision, not a gage decision. If the domain is shortened to 1.90 m, rescale the gage heights (core/surface 1.20 -> ~0.95, gage_low 0.15 -> unchanged, gage_low_mid 0.50 -> unchanged).
metadata._comment_ambient_bias: SUSPECTED BC ERROR, not fixed here. reference/civaux_sonde_ext.csv (the measured air temperature) runs 5-15 degC over 0-120 h, mean ~10 degC. All three robin BCs use a constant u_ref = 15 degC, i.e. roughly 5 K too warm. This biases the cooling branch and hits the near-surface gage (T_surface <-> sonde 4) hardest -- exactly the pair being validated. Fix by feeding sonde_ext in as a time_table u_ref before trusting any near-surface deviation metric.
metadata._comment_sonde5_time_axis: reference/civaux_sonde5.csv is labelled 'lift 2 core' but its data starts at 20 degC at t=0 and peaks at 20 h, i.e. a fresh-concrete signature on a t=0 axis. Lift 2 is cast at ~168 h, so this curve is either digitized on a LIFT-2-RELATIVE time axis or mis-attributed. Unusable against this model either way -- excluded from all curves and pairs.

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: thickness 1.2 m, height 1.9 m = levee 1 (95+95 cm, Fig. IV-11a). Section IV.A: 'un mur de 20 m de long et de 1,2 m d'epaisseur coule sur un radier'. The radier is NOT modelled here (adiabatic bottom) -- Briffaut meshes it, so expect the near-joint gage to run hot.

physical_groups.name: surface_left
physical_groups._comment: ASSUMED: left face, formwork or exposed. 6-value box, z padded ±1e-6.

physical_groups.name: surface_bottom
physical_groups._comment: ASSUMED: bottom on older concrete slab, treated as insulated (no BC = zero flux).

geometry._comment_convention: COORDINATE CONVENTION for all points below: x = through-thickness (0 = surface_left formwork face, 1.2 = surface_right formwork face, 0.6 = mid-thickness); y = height ABOVE THE FOUNDATION/WALL JOINT (y=0 IS the joint with the 40 cm radier, which is NOT meshed; y=2.4 = top surface). 'Depth' below always means distance to the NEAREST lateral (formwork) face. Mesh element_size = 0.05 m, so every gage snaps to the nearest node on the 0.05 m grid.

points.name: gage_core
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sonde 3 at (60, 95) cm -- core, mid-height of levee 1. Fig. IV-11a, Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

points.name: gage_surface
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sonde 4 at (10, 95) cm -- 10 cm from the left face, mid-height. Fig. IV-11a, Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

points.name: gage_low
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sonde 2 at (60, 20) cm -- 20 cm above the foundation, centreline. Fig. IV-11a, Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

points.name: gage_low_mid
points._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sonde 6 at (60, 180) cm -- 10 cm below the top of levee 1, centreline. Fig. IV-11a, Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

mesh._comment: ASSUMED: 0.05 m → 24 elements across 1.2 m thickness. Sufficient for smooth thermal gradient.

solid_mechanics._comment: DIMENSION PIN ONLY: this benchmark is pure thermo-chemo (no mechanics). Declared here per skill's 2D scalar-only trap rule so the physics dimension resolves to 2, matching the 2D mesh. NOT listed in assignment.active_fields — gets no DOFs, no kernel, no material section needed.

temperature._comment_k: PAPER_VALUE: 'Conductivite : 2.8 W/(m.K)' -- Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.
temperature._comment_rho: DERIVED: sum of the B11 mix (769+303+769 granulats + 350 ciment + 195 eau + 1.22 adjuvant) = 2387 kg/m3 -- Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.
temperature._comment_cp: PAPER_VALUE: 'Capacite massique : 950 J/(kg.K)' -- Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

degree_of_hydration._comment_B1: MISSING/CALIBRATE: affinity kinetics for the Civaux cement not given in Chapter 7. B1=3.6e-4 s⁻¹ (≈1.3 h⁻¹) is a plausible CEM I starting point — must be calibrated against Fig. 7.1 peak timing (~30-40 h) and magnitude. RISKY.
degree_of_hydration._comment_alpha_inf: ASSUMED: 0.85 typical for w/c ~0.45-0.50 CEM I (Waller 2000); w/c not given.
degree_of_hydration._comment_eta: GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE: 6.0 typical CEM I affinity model.
degree_of_hydration._comment_Ea: PAPER_VALUE: Tableau IV-3, 36583.8 J/mol -- Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.
degree_of_hydration._comment_Hu: GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE: 470 J/g, within 400-500 J/g for CEM I.
degree_of_hydration._comment_c_cement: PAPER_VALUE: 'Ciment Airvault CPA 55 350 kg' for Maquette B11 (= the 'voile BO' simulated) -- Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.
degree_of_hydration._comment_sanity: CROSS-CHECK vs Tableau IV-3 'Chaleur latente d'hydratation = 137000 kJ/m3': Hu*c_cement*alpha_inf = 470e3*350*0.85 = 139825 kJ/m3, i.e. +2.1%. The total heat is therefore right; B1/B2 (affinity KINETICS) remain uncalibrated -- Briffaut fits a 7-coefficient polynomial (a..g, Tableau IV-3), not the Cervera B1/B2/eta form used here.

initial_conditions._comment: ASSUMED: casting temperature 20°C = 293.15 K. Not stated in Chapter 7. HIGH IMPACT if wrong by >5°C.

boundary_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: formwork (2 cm wood), h=26.25 kJ/(h.m2.K) = 7.29 W/(m2.K). CONSTANT: Annexe C states the formwork was 'maintenu tout au long des releves de temperatures' -- there is NO stripping event. u_ref: sonde_ext measures 4.5-21 degC, time-weighted mean 9.7 -> 10 degC. A measured time_table is gated on the oofem backend (time-varying robin u_ref unverified), so a constant is used. Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

A measured time_table is gated on the oofem backend (time-varying robin u_ref unverified), so a constant is used. Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

A measured time_table is gated on the oofem backend (time-varying robin u_ref unverified), so a constant is used. Briffaut 2010 thesis (tel-00597072), Annexe C 'Donnees simulation mur Civaux'.

concrete_domain._comment: displacement NOT listed — it exists in physics only as a dimension pin, never gets DOFs.

time_stepping._comment_t_end: PAPER_VALUE: Fig. 7.1 x-axis goes to ~140 h = 504000 s.

results._comment_sonde_map: PROBE ASSIGNMENT (positions are read off the scaled sketch in Briffaut Fig. IV-11a / CEOS Fig. 1-8; the source gives NO coordinate table, so all placements are relative). Validation pairs: sonde 3 <-> gage_core, sonde 4 <-> gage_surface. Diagnostics only (NOT paired): sonde 1 <-> gage_low, sonde 2 <-> gage_low_mid, sonde_ext = ambient air. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: sonde 5 (core of LIFT 2 -- lift 2 is cast at ~168 h, which is beyond t_end = 504000 s = 140 h AND is not present in this single-block mesh, so no query can represent it); sondes 6/7 (edge/interface points whose location cannot be pinned from the figure -- no gage claims them).

reference_curves.label: Sonde 4 — Lift 1, near-surface (a few cm inside lateral formwork)
Sonde 1 — Lift 1 base, at foundation joint (DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — unreliable)
Sonde 2 — Lift 1, low (between joint and core) (DIAGNOSTIC ONLY)
Sonde ext — ambient AIR temperature (NOT a concrete value)
reference_curves._comment: Never pair this with a field query. Plotted only to expose the BC bias: measured air runs ~5-15 degC (mean ~10 degC), while every robin BC in this model uses u_ref = 15 degC. See metadata._comment_ambient_bias.

queries.label: Core temperature [°C]
queries._comment_units: Field solves in degC (IC/u_ref are degC; only degree_of_hydration.T_ref is Kelvin) -- no K->C conversion.

queries.label: Near-surface temperature [°C]
queries._comment_units: Field solves in degC (IC/u_ref are degC; only degree_of_hydration.T_ref is Kelvin) -- no K->C conversion.
queries._comment_pairing: Paired with sonde 4. Renamed from 'Surface temperature': the gage is 6 cm INSIDE the face, and no probe sits on the skin.

queries.label: Base temperature, 0.15 m above joint [°C]
queries._comment_units: Field solves in degC (IC/u_ref are degC; only degree_of_hydration.T_ref is Kelvin) -- no K->C conversion.
queries._comment_pairing: DIAGNOSTIC vs sonde 1 -- deliberately NOT in reference_deviation.pairs. The adiabatic bottom omits the cold 40 cm radier, so a large positive bias here is EXPECTED and is the point of the query.

queries.label: Lower-lift temperature, 0.50 m above joint [°C]
queries._comment_units: Field solves in degC (IC/u_ref are degC; only degree_of_hydration.T_ref is Kelvin) -- no K->C conversion.
queries._comment_pairing: DIAGNOSTIC vs sonde 2 -- deliberately NOT in reference_deviation.pairs. Probe height is a guess; same adiabatic-bottom caveat as T_low.

plots.name: temperature_history
plots.title: Civaux Wall - Temperature History (Fig. 7.1)
plots._comment: VALIDATION plot. Curve order mirrors reference_deviation.pairs exactly: T_core<->sonde 3, T_surface<->sonde 4. Do not add sonde 1/2/5/ext here -- they belong in temperature_diagnostic.

plots.name: temperature_diagnostic
plots.title: Civaux Wall — Lower-lift diagnostics (foundation heat sink NOT modelled)
plots._comment: DIAGNOSTIC plot, NOT a validation target. Expect the two FEM curves to sit well ABOVE sondes 1 and 2: the model has no foundation and an adiabatic bottom, so the radier heat sink that damps both probes is absent. The gap is a direct measure of that omission. The ambient curve shows the measured air is ~5-15 degC, not the assumed u_ref = 15 degC.

reference_deviation._comment: ONLY physically defensible pairs belong here. gage_core is the deepest point in the section <-> sonde 3, the hottest/earliest probe and the CEOS reference point for lift 1. gage_surface is 6 cm inside the formwork face at the SAME height <-> sonde 4, whose 6 K lower / 10 h later peak is the near-surface signature. Sonde 1 is NOT usable as a target (it reads the cold radier, which this mesh does not contain) and sonde 5 is lift 2 (never cast within t_end) -- both are excluded on purpose; see results._comment_sonde_map.
